source.title: Forward Compatible Training for Large-Scale Embedding Retrieval Systems
source.authors: V. Ramanujan; Pavan Kumar Anasosalu Vasu; Ali Farhadi; O. Tuzel; H. Pouransari

record.file_problem: none; the paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests V4 by measuring retrieval compatibility after a learned transformation, rather than measuring representational convergence directly.
record.gate_note: The study tests a trained mapping for visual retrieval compatibility, not whether independently trained representations naturally converge with scale. Its CKA analysis compares old-model features with side-information to assess complementarity, not convergence between models, so that result is not recorded as a row.
record.test_reason: A retrieval-compatibility method paper. Its no-side-information ablations (ψ=0) directly measure how well an MLP maps one independently trained model's embeddings onto another's, across architectures, datasets and losses. This bears on V4 in a new setting (top-1 retrieval after mapping). Its linear CKA between two seeds of the old model bears weakly on V3. The main FCT rows map old embeddings plus extra side-information features, so they test the authors' method rather than V4 itself.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that FCT, a learned transformation plus stored side-information, gives old/new embedding compatibility across datasets, architectures and losses without degrading the independently trained new model. They stress that side-information, best learned contrastively, is needed because a direct old→new transformation cannot recover information the old model discarded. They also list cross-domain compatibility as untested.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes forward-compatible training and a learned MLP transformation using old embeddings plus side-information; it does not reproduce a representation-similarity method from the cited original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: Compatibility changes with side-information choice, embedding architecture and dimension, training-data/domain setting, and sequential versus direct update path.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding auxiliary self-supervised (SimCLR) features to old embeddings improves old→new mapping (65.0 vs 61.8 on ImageNet). SimCLR features have low CKA (0.27) with the supervised old model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Features from a different objective are complementary to a supervised model's, and combining them improves cross-model embedding transfer.

fits_no_version.finding: BCT-trained new models, made compatible on purpose, reach lower cross-model retrieval than FCT (46.9 vs 65.0 on ImageNet).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Induced backward compatibility costs new-model accuracy; this is a method comparison, not convergence.

record.problems: Compatibility is evaluated indirectly through retrieval rather than a representation-alignment metric. The mapping is deliberately trained using new-model training data, and results are specific to visual retrieval; no uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported retrieval-compatibility results were left out.

untested.parts: No scale or capability sweep of alignment between independently trained models.
No vision-language or paired image-caption models.
Only one linear CKA number between two seeds (0.70). No feature-level, unit-level or subspace matching.
Only nonlinear MLP maps (about 5.7M params) trained on paired new-model data were tested. Linear maps, stitching, relative representations and unpaired mapping were not tested.
No comparison of similarity measures or their settings.
No test of what causes alignment or whether it plateaus.

missing.what: No-side-info sequential maps: two-hop 44.9%, direct v1→v3 53.9%, vs φ3/φ3 68.1%
Mapping from SimCLR features alone (no φold) to new model: 63.2% top-1
Linear CKA old vs alternate-seed old model 0.70; vs Mixup variant 0.66; vs SimCLR 0.27

record.verdict_notes: Most of the record's rows measure the authors' method (FCT with side-information) or BCT and do not bear on V4 as stated; only the ψ=0 ablations do. Row r18 has the wrong value (34.8%, not 31.9%), and r11 mislabels a single-hop result as sequential. In every setting the old model is trained on less data than the new one, so part of the mapping loss reflects an information gap rather than failed convergence. The study cites Convergent Learning but is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: No scale or capability sweep measuring alignment between independently trained models.
An alternate initialization is used as side-information, but shared features or subspaces across seeds are not measured.

Tests learned nonlinear transformations for retrieval, generally using side-information and training data for the new model. Does not test a linear-only map, stitching, relative representations, or mapping without paired training examples.
No recurring interpretable features or circuits are measured.
Does not compare representation-similarity measures, their settings, or input choices as measures of convergence.
Although some models use different data or objectives, the study evaluates learned mappings rather than whether natural alignment is incomplete or caused by shared training.

relationships.condition: Single-hop pure old→new MLP map (no side-information), Places in-domain and ImageNet→Places disjoint training data
relationships.reason: Mapping lifts cross-model retrieval from ~0.3% to within 2-4 points of new/new (r18 34.8 vs 37.0; r21 33.3 vs 37.0).
relationships.display_finding: Mapping raised cross-model retrieval from about 0.3% to 34.8% in-domain and 33.3% with disjoint training data, versus 37.0% for new-model self-retrieval.

relationships.condition: ImageNet-500→1k and VGGFace2 pure maps; chained updates; map type
relationships.reason: Larger losses: r13 61.8 vs 68.1, r19 91.5 vs 96.6. Text: two-hop map without side-info falls to 44.9% (Table 8). The map needs a trained nonlinear MLP, and the authors argue old embeddings discard information the new model needs.
relationships.display_finding: Mapped performance reached 61.8 versus 68.1 on ImageNet and 91.5 versus 96.6 on VGGFace2, while two-hop mapping without side information fell to 44.9%, despite using a trained nonlinear MLP.

relation.reason: The study directly measures retrieval compatibility after mapping independently trained embeddings, and reports cross-seed representation similarity.

tranche.reason: The no-side-information ablations test representation interchangeability in a retrieval-system update setting, including changes in training data and architecture.

source_check.notes: The no-side-information rows directly inform V4 despite their control roles. Compatibility is measured through nearest-neighbor retrieval after a trained nonlinear MLP; linear-map sufficiency and arbitrary downstream interchangeability remain untested.
